paper_id: Ma et al. - 2015 - Sherlock Is Around Detecting Network Failures with Local Evidence Fusion
title: Sherlock Is Around: Detecting Network Failures with Local Evidence Fusion
motivation: Sink-based diagnosis incurs huge transmission overhead; sink fails to obtain complete evidence from problematic regions.
problem_framing: Balance diagnosis workload among sensor nodes while guaranteeing integrated judgment with consistent results.
key_insight: Root causes can be partly reflected by nodes within a neighborhood; local fusion achieves high accuracy without long-distance evidence collection.
method_signature: Local-Diagnosis (LD2): Naive Bayesian Classifier + Dempster-Shafer evidence fusion via dynamically constructed fusion tree.
evaluation_criteria: False negative rate (miss detection), false positive rate (false alarm), time cost on 50-node TelosB testbed.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: D-S theory fails when evidences are highly conflicting; must reduce impact of incorrect and fringe evidences.
evidence_for_taste: sink often fails to obtain complete evidences
thinking_moves: 把诊断负担从sink分布式化到邻居节点
用D-S理论融合局部证据,确保融合结果与顺序无关(associative law)
邻居节点数增加→诊断准确率提升的自然单调性
为避免Heisenbug,诊断过程本身不能引入过多通信开销
